umentemque: ūmēns (ūmidus), -entis — damp, dank, dewy (m./f. acc. sg.; from ūmeō) + -que 'and'
una: ūnus, -a, -um — one, a single (f. abl./nom. sg.); ūnā (adv.), together · also ūnā, adv., once (satis ūnā superque, enough once and more)
urbes: urbs, urbis (f.) — city (nom. pl.; also acc. pl.)
vacua: vacuus, -a, -um — empty, deserted, unguarded (n. nom./acc. pl.; f. nom./abl. sg.)
vagatur: vagor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to wander, roam, spread abroad (3rd sg. pres., deponent)
vana: vānus, -a, -um — empty, false, idle (f. abl. sg.; f. nom. sg.; n. nom./acc. pl.)
vel: vel (conj., adv.) — or; even; vel… vel, either… or
veniam: venia, -ae (f.) — favour, grace, pardon, leave (acc. sg.)
venis: veniō, venīre, vēnī, ventum — to come (2nd sg. pres.)
venit: veniō, venīre, vēnī — to come (3rd sg. perf. vēnit, or pres. venit)
vero: vērō (adv.) — in truth, indeed, but; tum vērō, then indeed
veteris: vetus, veteris — old, aged (m./n. gen. sg.)
vincla: vinc(u)lum, -ī (n.) — chain, bond, fetter (nom./acc. pl., shortened form of vincula)
viri: vir, virī (m.) — man, hero, husband (nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also voc. pl. (festīnāte, virī)
volnus: vulnus (volnus), vulneris (n.) — wound (acc./nom. sg.; older spelling)
voltus: vultus (voltus), -ūs (m.) — face, look, expression (nom. sg.; acc. pl.)
vota: vōtum, -ī (n.) — vow, promise to a god, prayer (acc./nom. pl.)
